title: Life Cycles
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Life Cycles Worksheets (Mammal, Amphibian, Insect and Bird)
standard_code: Year 5: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Describe the differences in the life cycles of a mammal, an amphibian, an insect and a bird.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on life cycles: mammals, amphibians, insects and birds, metamorphosis, the order of stages and gestation times. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Every animal has a life cycle.
key_sub: Mammals, birds, amphibians and insects grow up in different ways.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things have a life cycle, but the stages differ.

  • Mammal: born live, fed on milk, grows into an adult. Bird: hard-shelled egg kept warm, chick, adult.
  • Amphibian: jelly eggs in water → tadpole → froglet → adult (metamorphosis).
  • Insect: egg → larva → pupa → adult (complete), or egg → nymph → adult (incomplete).
Example

After the caterpillar comes?

Egg → caterpillar → chrysalis → butterfly

Answer: the chrysalis (pupa)

Example

Elephant 22 months, human 9 months. Difference?

22 − 9

Answer: 13 months

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all animals lay eggs.
  • Thinking a tadpole is a fish.
  • Thinking every insect has a pupa stage.

faq.a: Mammals give birth to live young; birds lay hard-shelled eggs; amphibians start as tadpoles in water; many insects change completely from larva to pupa to adult.
A big change in body shape during the life cycle, such as a tadpole turning into a frog or a caterpillar turning into a butterfly.
The time a baby mammal grows inside its mother, from about 2 months for a cat to about 22 months for an elephant.
